status.en: 303 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 15% fewer than the week before, most of them in Delhi, Mumbai and Hyderabad.
status.nb: 303 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 15 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Delhi, Mumbai og Hyderabad.

summary.en: In the past seven days 303 armed incidents were reported, 15% fewer than the previous week, concentrated in Delhi, Mumbai and Hyderabad, and 37 of them were carried by two or more outlets. The UCDP recorded 437 battle‑related deaths in 2024. In Manipur fresh Kuki‑Naga clashes left nine dead across three hill districts, prompting the chief minister to appeal for peace. Delhi is bracing for further protests as the released “cockroach” movement leaders spark renewed tension.
summary.nb: I løpet av de siste syv dagene ble 303 væpnede hendelser rapportert, 15 % færre enn uken før, hovedsakelig i Delhi, Mumbai og Hyderabad, og 37 av dem ble dekket av to eller flere medier. UCDP registrerte 437 kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2024. I Manipur førte nye Kuki‑Naga‑konflikter til ni døde i tre fjellområder, og guvernøren oppfordrer til fred. Delhi forbereder seg på flere protester etter at de løslatte “kakerlak‑”bevegelseslederne har skapt ny spenning.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
